title: John Eglinton’s carping voice asked.
html_source:
John Eglington is distinguished from Lyster, Russell and Best throughout the start of this chapter by the use of staid statements about him. So far, there have been ten references to him.
John Eglington asked with elder’s gall.
John Eglington censured.
John Eglington sedately said.
John Eglington, frowning , said.
John Eglington opined.
John Eglington newgathered frown.
John Eglington said for Mr. Best’s behoof.
John Eglington shifted his spare body, leaning back to judge.
John Eglinton’s carping voice asked.

Compare this to George Russell, known as AE, who is referred heretofore as he or Russell by Joyce.
-his rufous skull….
- Russell oracled out of his…
-Russell began impatiently

Eglington is mentioned 30 times in Scylla and Charybdis the vast majority include both fore and surname. Ellmann reports that Joyce did poke fun at WK Magee, Eglinton’s real name, Eglinton being Magee’s nom de plume. This is repeated in reference number 26 to Eglinton in Scylla and Charybdis ‘He laughed, unmarried, at Eglinton Johannes, of arts a bachelor.’
